payload.title: Record session-task links in the ledger by session UUID
payload.description: Record session UUIDs alongside local ES numbers in ledger event actors, and record session_tasks events in the ledger keyed by UUID, so any machine can see which past sessions worked on a task and group tasks by session.
payload.context:
Sessions are machine data and stay out of the project ledger. Ledger actors today carry only the local ES number (session_id), which means nothing on another machine and collides across machines. session_tasks rows are live-only: nothing replays them, so a rebuild or another machine loses which sessions touched a task, including non-mutating interest such as touch.

Agreed with Mike while reconciling E-2291 (EQ-93): carry the UUID and the ES number side by side; never replace the ES number. The machine that ran a session keeps showing ES-NNNN with its transcript link.

Open design point — display width: task show's Sessions: block aligns sessions in a narrow column (ES-1276, 7 characters). A session from another machine has no local ES row, so it needs an equally concise form, e.g. a short UUID prefix (ES~7844f), with the host shown in a legend or in session show rather than inline.

Out of scope, a maybe for later: capturing transcripts themselves (compressed binary, explicit opt-in per project) for teams that want to see why something happened. Transcripts are large, can hold secrets, and do not belong in git history by default.

payload.title: Capture session transcripts as opt-in project data
payload.description: Capture session transcripts into a project as compressed binary, opt-in per project, so a team can see why a change happened the way it did, from any machine.
payload.context: Transcripts live only on the machine that ran the session, so another machine or teammate cannot see the reasoning behind a change. Agreed with Mike while reconciling E-2291: transcripts are large, can hold pasted secrets, and do not belong in a project's git history by default, so capture must be an explicit opt-in. Storage would likely be compressed binary. Some teams will want it to learn why something happened as it did. Pairs with recording session-task links in the ledger by session UUID, which gives a transcript a cross-machine identity to attach to.

  - `E-M` picks the present session that claimed E-M. With no present session, or more than one, it refuses and names the sessions, with the `ES-N` form to use.
  - `ES-N` names the session directly.
  - The chosen session is touched for E-N (upgrade-only, so a stronger relation stays), and its hide of E-N, if any, is cleared, so the task is on its board.
  - `none` deletes the row.
- The claiming session may be chosen.

## Working out the steward
- One Go function in `internal/monitor`, shared by the boards (`session_stewardship.go`) and the commands below: the stored steward when its session is present and has not hidden the task; otherwise the existing rules (filer, else the only editor, claimer and hiders not counted, two at the deciding step is ambiguous).
- It is the same answer whichever session is looking.
- Exposed to Python through an `endless-go` subcommand, so Python reads no SQLite.

## Commands that show it
- `endless task steward E-N`: prints `ES-N` alone on stdout. With no steward it prints nothing on stdout, says so on stderr, and exits non-zero; when ambiguous it does the same and names the candidates.
- `endless session goto --steward E-N`: goes to that session, refusing as `task steward` does when there is none.

- `session unhide --task` on a task that is not hidden refuses, and names `endless session touch E-N`.

fields.context:
A task's steward (ED-1605) is the session whose board keeps a task in view so the user remembers to work on it and spawn it. Today stewardship is worked out every time a board is drawn and never stored. The steward is the present session that filed the task; failing that, the only present session that edited it. The task's claiming session is not counted, a session that hid the task is not counted, and two candidates at the deciding step leave the task ambiguous, with no steward.

Today the only way to see a task's steward is to open boards and look. The only way to change it is per board: `session hide --task` takes a task off one session's board, and `session unhide --task` on a task that is not hidden writes a pin (E-2293) that keeps the task on that board as well. A pin does not make the session the steward. ## Decisions taken while planning (with the user, 2026-10-20)

- **The chosen steward is stored (Q1 C).** Two alternatives were rejected. Making a touch outrank filing fails because the user touches a task only to see it, without meaning that session to steward it. Hiding the task on every other candidate leaves no steward once the chosen session ends, because the hides keep the filer out.
- **A stored steward counts only while its session is present** and has not hidden the task. Otherwise the steward is worked out as before, so stewardship still corrects itself when the chosen session ends, and comes back to it if that session is resumed.
- **The claiming session alone gives "none" (Q2 A).** The steward and the owner are different things (ED-1605); `session goto E-N` already reaches the owner.
- **`--steward none` clears the stored choice.** The steward is worked out again, as if `--steward` had never been set. A stored "no steward" was considered and not adopted.
- **Pins are retired here (ED-1633).** A touched task is never suppressed by another session's stewardship, so a pin has nothing left to override.

It proposed setting the steward by pinning the task on the chosen session and hiding it everywhere else. A pin never made a session the steward: the steward is worked out only from filing and editing. So `task steward` would have reported no steward whenever the chosen session had not filed or edited the task.

Hides and pins are per-(session, task) rows written through `session_tasks.*` events (`internal/events/session_task_visibility.go`). The stored steward is one row per task, written the same way through its own event, so it replays from the ledger like a hide.

payload.title: Add a command that moves a task's worktree to its project
payload.description: Add a command that moves a task's worktree into another registered project's repository and retires the old worktree, branch and sandbox, refusing when the old branch holds work it cannot carry over safely.
payload.context:
E-2349 was spawned into go-cfgstore although the task belongs to endless, so its worktree (`go-cfgstore/.endless/worktrees/e-2349`, branch `task/2349`, plus a sandbox database) was cut from the wrong repository. E-2405 now stops spawn and claim from doing this, but a worktree already created in the wrong repository has no supported way out: `worktree drop` leaves the sandbox (E-1332), and nothing re-creates the worktree in the right repository.

Mike proposed `endless worktree move <task_id> --to=<project_slug>`.

Limits found while filing:
- A git worktree belongs to one repository, so a "move" is: create the worktree in the target repository, carry the work over, then retire the old worktree, branch and sandbox. It can be done reliably when the source branch has no commits beyond its base and no uncommitted changes. When it has work, that work is commits on another repository's history; carrying it over is a patch apply that can fail, so the safe default is to refuse and name what is there.
- Task events the wrong project already recorded in its own ledger (as E-2405's P11 found for E-2208) would also need to move, and the ledger is never hand-edited, so the command needs an event-pipeline way to do it, or it refuses when such events exist.
- With E-2405 in place, the target is the task's own project, so `--to` may be unnecessary unless the command should also re-home the task itself.

ops.statement: go-cfgstore's mistaken e-2349 worktree, its task/2349 branch and its sandbox database are gone, and nothing under go-cfgstore still refers to E-2349's worktree

payload.answer: Commit Endless-owned files (config.json, .endless/tasks/CLAUDE.md, _harness.sh, _guard.sh) always. Commit Endless's edits to user-owned files (.gitignore, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md) only when that file had no uncommitted changes before the run; otherwise leave it and say so.

ops.statement: Project init always commits the Endless-owned files it changed, and commits its edits to .gitignore, CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md only when that file had no uncommitted change before the run, listing what it left out

fields.plan:
# Bring a registered project up to Endless usage

All code is in the `endless` repo. Python owns the CLI and the file work
(`src/endless/`); Go owns the database (`internal/monitor` holds the queries,
`internal/projectcmd` dispatches the `endless-go project <verb>` verbs), and
Python reaches Go through `event_bridge.project_registry`.

Where a choice is the user's, this plan names a recommended default and the
task carries the question (listed under Open questions); an answer other than the default changes only the
section that names it.

## The bring-up command: `endless project init`, re-run

Recommended default: no new verb. `project init` (alias `register`) is already
idempotent — `register_project` merges `.endless/config.json`,
`scaffold_gitignore` appends only missing lines, `scaffold_suite_rules` never
overwrites — and it is the command a user already knows. This task extends it so
that running it on a project registered at any earlier time brings that project
fully up to date, and running it again changes nothing.

`register.register_project`, in order:

1. **Refuse a worktree** (new, before anything is written): refuse when the
   target is a git linked worktree (`git rev-parse --git-dir` differs from
   `--git-common-dir`) or lies under a registered project's
   `.endless/worktrees/`. The refusal names the owning project. This does not
   depend on the row's `identity` column, which E-2217's duplicate check needs
   and older rows may lack.
2. Existing steps, unchanged: ignore marker, identity, duplicate and name
   checks, the config merge, the DB row.
3. **Gitignore** (`scaffold_gitignore`): `GITIGNORE_ENTRIES` gains
   `.endless/logs/`, where `internal/monitor/session_notices.go`
   `AppendNoticeLog` writes `session-notices.jsonl`.
4. **Suite rules** (`scaffold_suite_rules`): unchanged.
5. **Harness** (new, `suite_rules.scaffold_harness`): write `_harness.sh` and
   `_guard.sh` into `<project>/.endless/tasks/`, writing a file only when it is
   missing or its bytes differ from the shipped copy (they are Endless's files,
   not the project's, so a stale copy is replaced; EQ-84).
6. **Agent-instructions pointer** (new, `register.scaffold_guide_pointer`): if
   the project root has neither `CLAUDE.md` nor `AGENTS.md`, create `CLAUDE.md`
   holding a short block that tells an agent to run `endless guide` first. If
   either exists and neither mentions `endless guide`, append the same block,
   under a marker line, to `CLAUDE.md` if present, else `AGENTS.md`. A file
   that already mentions `endless guide` is left alone.
7. **Commit** (new; whether to commit at all is EQ-83). Before step 2 runs,
   record `git status --porcelain` for the candidate paths:
   `.endless/config.json`, `.endless/tasks/CLAUDE.md`, the two harness files
   (Endless-owned), and `.gitignore`, `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` (user-owned).
   After step 6, the commit set is every candidate path that is now modified
   or untracked, minus any path that was *modified or staged* before the run
   (the user had work in it). An Endless-owned path that was *untracked* before
   the run is committed — that is the legacy case of a `config.json` that was
   never committed. A user-owned path that was untracked before the run is not
   committed (it is the user's uncommitted file). If the checkout is not on its
   default branch, the commit set is empty. Commit the set with one pathspec
   commit (message `Endless: bring project up to Endless usage`), then print
   every changed path left out and why. An empty set commits nothing.

Idempotence follows from each step writing only what is missing or different,
and step 7 committing only what changed.

## Harness source of truth

`_harness.sh` and `_guard.sh` move into the Python package as package data
(`src/endless/data/tasks/`), read with `importlib.resources`. The endless repo's
own `.endless/tasks/` copies are produced by running step 5 on the endless repo
itself, like any other project, and a test asserts the committed copies are
byte-identical to the package data, so editing one without the other fails the
suite.

## Land does not mistake Endless's runtime files for user work

The task's notes ask for this, and E-2363, which asked for it alone, was
superseded into this task: without it, the first land after bring-up in a repo
whose `.gitignore` predates an entry is refused. `worktree_cmd._git_status_partition`
gets a third class, Endless runtime paths, taken from `GITIGNORE_ENTRIES`
(shared, not copied), which land neither commits nor counts as user work.

## A clean way to drop a mistaken registration

`internal/monitor` gains `DeleteProjectRow`, which deletes a project's row by
path; `internal/projectcmd` gains a `delete` verb that calls it; Python reaches
it through `event_bridge.project_registry("delete", path)`. A new `project`
verb in `cli.py` (recommended name `forget`, EQ-86) calls it. It writes nothing to the
project's `.endless/config.json` and adds nothing to the ignore list, unlike
`project unregister`, which does both. Recommended default for a row that has
tasks: refuse, naming the count, since
deleting would orphan task history (EQ-87).

## Apply it to go-cfgstore

After it lands, run `endless project init` in go-cfgstore's main checkout so it
gains `.endless/logs/` in `.gitignore`, the harness, and the commit.

## Fold-in

`task_cmd._report_gate_on`'s docstring says the minimizer defaults on; E-2373
made the default off. Correct it.

## Out of scope

- The minimizer block: since E-2373 a missing block means off, so bring-up has
  nothing to write.
- Porting a Makefile to a justfile: that is the user's repo policy, not
  something Endless knows how to do for an arbitrary project. It is done per
  repo (go-cfgstore's was done in E-2206).
- Health checks and reporting: `endless doctor` (E-2287) owns those.

## Open questions (asked on the task as EQ-81..EQ-88)

The defaults above are recommendations, not decisions; each is asked:

- EQ-81 (answered: an endless worktree): where the work happens — this task belongs to `endless`, but its
  worktree was cut in go-cfgstore.
- EQ-82 (answered): `project init` re-run; `doctor --fix` later calls the same steps.
- EQ-83 (answered): Endless-owned files always; user-owned only when clean before the run.
- EQ-84: replace a differing `_harness.sh`/`_guard.sh`, or leave and report.
- EQ-85: append the guide pointer to an existing CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, or only
  create a missing file.
- EQ-86: the drop verb's name.
- EQ-87: what the drop verb does with a row that has tasks, and what it points
  at instead of `project unregister`.
- EQ-88: who removes the two temporary lines in go-cfgstore's
  `.git/info/exclude`.

## Tests

- `tests/test_register.py`: gitignore entries; the guard that every
  uncommitted runtime path under `.endless/` that Go writes is in
  `GITIGNORE_ENTRIES`; the worktree refusal writing nothing; the guide pointer
  in each of its three cases; the commit rule (clean default branch commits,
  dirty or non-default reports); a project registered the old way brought up
  to date, then a second run changing no file and creating no commit.
- `tests/test_suite_rules.py`: harness install, replace-when-different, and the
  package-data/committed-copy identity check.
- A worktree-land test for the runtime-path class.
- `internal/monitor` Go test for `DeleteProjectRow`, `internal/projectcmd` test
  for the verb, and a Python CLI test for `project forget`.
- The task's `verify.sh` runs these plus one end-to-end bring-up of a fixture
  repo registered the old way, run twice.
